correctness.rationale: For the stated integral multiplication and n>=2, e_1 generates the algebra, so a derivation is determined by its value on e_1. In the derivation identity, after factoring out (a+b+h-2)!/((a-1)! b! h!), the left side has factor a+b+h-1 and the two right sides have factors a+h-1 and b. This verifies the identity over the integers and hence over any field; truncation preserves it by degree. The indicated maps extend the arbitrary generator images, and their brackets follow by evaluating on e_1. Fixing a partner, distinct basis terms have distinct output degrees, so no mixed central term can survive by cancellation. The partner 1 forces i=1 in characteristic 0 or i=1 modulo p in characteristic p. Partner 2 rules out i=1 in characteristic 0 and all such i<n for odd p; the top degree is then central exactly as stated. In characteristic 2, for odd i with s trailing ones, Lucas carry tests give both binomial coefficients even for 2<=j<2^s, both odd at j=1, and exactly one odd at j=2^s. Thus centrality means the first nonzero partner is beyond the cutoff. With N=n+1 the inequalities for i=2^s(2u+1)-1 say that digit s of N must be one and its remainder modulo 2^s at most 2^s-2. These are exactly one-bits above the trailing run, of length nu_2(n+2), including the no-admissible-bits case. At n=2^r-3 this gives r-1. The 360 finite cases reported in the inspected checker and verification notes are corroboration; the uploaded script was not executed.
